surprises.head: The Rangers couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: The Rangers usually get better looks than most teams. Not tonight: a 4.7% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.6% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Luke Hughes scores twice as the Devils beat the Rangers
paras: An ugly night for the Rangers. Luke Hughes, who scores in about 1 game in 11, scored twice. Will Cuylle and Johnathan Kovacevic fought midway through the first, and Evan Rodrigues opened the scoring for the Devils with 30 seconds left in the period. The second period belonged to the Devils. Luke Hughes, Nico Hischier and Arseny Gritsyuk scored three goals in less than five minutes early in the period to make it 4-0. The Rangers pulled Dylan Garand after four goals and turned to Spencer Martin for the rest of the second. Luke Hughes scored again late in the second to make it 5-0 for the Devils, and Stefan Noesen made it 6-0 early in the third. Pavel Dorofeyev got the Rangers on the board on the power play just over a minute later, far too late to matter. Cody Glass stretched the lead to 7-1 shorthanded with just over five minutes left.

The Devils drove the play, outshooting the Rangers 31-19 (26-12 at 5-on-5), and the scoreboard caught up. Nico Daws made 18 saves for the Devils. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Dougie Hamilton, by our Swing measure.

Marcus Pettersson took three penalties on his own. Alexis Lafrenière picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Rangers killed off a two-man advantage that lasted two minutes midway through the first. The Devils moved to 4-3-0 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Rangers fell to 6-3-0, second in the Metropolitan.
